delta.adapter: Adds one test adapter at the private fixture/consumer boundary. It invokes actual LIVE_INSTALL once into a stack-local response, logs actual returned NTSTATUS and response status/identity/flags for the observer, and returns only monotone elapsed completion under four seconds.
delta.consumer: CHECK12 uses adapter completion; a fresh ordinary LIVE_SNAPSHOT replaces the previous reuse of the INSTALL response for model/page observations. On the qualified path, CANCEL and the actual SAFE/model-absence/producer-SAFE/cleanup sequence remain unchanged.
delta.other_changes: JSON type, private window-class name, Root title, and check labels. Polling and all failure cleanup/exit logic are unchanged.

assessments.result: The adapter sets a real correctly shaped LIVE_INSTALL request and calls the existing fixture exactly once. It does not overwrite a kernel/USER/fixture return value or interpret observed NTSTATUS/response.status as success. The response remains local; only raw observer logging consumes its fields. CHECK12 depends on timely adapter completion. CHECK13/14 depend on a new successful bounded SNAPSHOT, actual Cocoa model1/context ownership, and a readable non-SAFE host page rather than the local INSTALL result.

assessments.topic: Known ownership before the unconsumed response
assessments.result: Before entering the adapter, the unchanged successful SETUP/PREPARE and CHECK9/11 establish the real exported context, producer owner, known ticket, and mapped readable RO host page. The saved lease/epoch/ticket are not replaced from the adapter response. Native ownership and its pre-send install-attempt latch remain in the previously admitted unchanged helper, so losing the local response does not discard those cleanup owners.

assessments.topic: Fresh witness and terminal permission before release
assessments.result: The fresh SNAPSHOT must qualify independently; failure records a failed check and exits to cleanup. Model observation requires actual attached/ledger/current counts1 and retained context; the host page must still be a valid snapshot. The qualified path always proceeds to known-ticket CANCEL independent of the local INSTALL status. It then requires actual HostSAFE with invalid dynamic values plus a valid zero model witness, unchanged saved identity and owned context, explicit producer RELEASE and actual ProducerSAFE, before local context/readers/window cleanup.

The adapter checks its starting clock before dispatch, and checks a single four-second elapsed budget after the actual call and raw JSON/flush. A late return can therefore fail CHECK12 after real side effects; the unchanged done path invokes ownership-aware helper cleanup rather than retrying INSTALL or assuming failure meant no import. The added SNAPSHOT has its own existing operation budget. Output failure sets io_error and cannot produce a successful final exit.

All25 numbered checks remain. The added conditional failed-SNAPSHOT check increments failure count and immediately exits, so it cannot inflate a successful25/0 count. Subsequent real NT closes, window destruction, module/class release, cleanup result, I/O error, exact check-count and exit predicates retain the admitted behavior. No new ownership transfer, asynchronous task, page writer, or cleanup shortcut is introduced.

report.admission_scope: Admit the supplied normal-case test of decision independence from the immediate INSTALL response, conditional on the unchanged qualified112 Native/PE helper/header artifacts. The consumer qualifies an actual installed-model snapshot and cancels its retained ticket without branching on the adapter-local INSTALL NTSTATUS or operation status.
limits: Only the two named client files were read for this delta. Previously admitted helper semantics supply context; Native/PE source, binaries, integration, controller, dependency closures, and runtime receipts were not re-audited or independently rebound.
No code edits, builds, tests, candidate execution, network, runtime control, or Windows/default changes. Only this requested JSON report was written.

No actual25/0 result, paired compile/runtime success, artifact match, or cleanup restoration receipt is claimed. Observer logs must remain bound to actual integrated artifacts and raw results by the parent.

This is deliberate application-test adapter non-consumption after a synchronous fixture call. It does not create or prove a genuine USER timeout, message drop, outstanding asynchronous request, kernel failure, or complete unknown-transport acceptance.

Decision independence is verified at the branch/use sites, not as opaque information isolation: the unchanged fresh diagnostic SNAPSHOT includes the helper last reply_status field and operation() logs it, but no consumer check branches on that field. Physical model observations intentionally provide information about effects.

The normal qualified path CANCELs after a timely adapter and successful model/page observation. Adapter lateness, failed SNAPSHOT, or failed model qualification exits to inherited producer-release cleanup; this source does not establish unconditional per-ticket CANCEL on every failure path.

The four-second guards reject late completion after return and cannot preempt blocked foreign calls or output. An external watchdog remains necessary. Inherited cleanup=true alone is not whole-server drain evidence after an earlier unknown ACQUIRE without a captured lease/reader.

No GPU/pixel/rendering, cross-process, NT-close-failure, protection, negative, or CANCEL-concurrency qualification; no blocked acceptance is replaced. Blocked partial files and parked cross-process drafts were not accessed, resumed, or retried.
